Monte Carlo uncertainty for a parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio p-value

pb_lrt_mc_error.Rd

Reports Monte Carlo uncertainty for the likelihood-ratio bootstrap exceedance probability, conditional on successful refits.

Usage

pb_lrt_mc_error(test, level = 0.95)

Arguments

test

A pb_lrt object returned by pb_lrt.

level

Confidence level for the exact binomial interval.

Details

The original bootstrap p-value \((1+k)/(1+B)\) is preserved, where \(k\) of the \(B\) valid bootstrap statistics exceed or equal the observed test statistic. The Monte Carlo standard error is the binomial plug-in estimate based on \(k/B\); the interval is the exact Clopper-Pearson interval for that exceedance probability. When \(k=0\), the plug-in standard error is zero but the interval has a positive upper limit. Failed refits are excluded. The interval does not cover model or parameter uncertainty and is conditional on the validity and independence of successful bootstrap replicates.

Value

A one-row data frame with p_value, exceedance_probability, mc_standard_error, lower, upper, exceedances, valid_replicates, and failed_replicates.

Examples

null <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
alt <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
test <- pb_lrt(null, alt, n = 30, seed = 1)
pb_lrt_mc_error(test)
#>      p_value exceedance_probability mc_standard_error lower     upper
#> 1 0.03225806                      0                 0     0 0.1157033
#>   exceedances valid_replicates failed_replicates
#> 1           0               30                 0
